rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they cannot answer the challenge, the Prophet’s truth is clear; they should believe rather than persist in denial and incur punishment.
rows.anchor: فإذا لم تعارضوه وبان عجزكم ووجب تصديقه فآمنوا وخافوا العذاب المعد لمن كذب وعاند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inimitable challenge establishes prophethood, and predicting they will never answer it is unseen knowledge known only to God.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليلا على إثبات النبوة صحة كون المتحدى به معجزا والاخبار بأنهم لن يفعلوا وهو غيب لا يعلمه إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because inability seemed doubtful to eloquent opponents, إن expresses their uncertainty rather than إذا, which signals certainty.
rows.anchor: لما كان العجز عن المعارضة قبل التأمل كالمشكوك فيه لديهم لا تكالهم على فصاحتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن is the conditional particle for doubt, unlike إذا for certainty, matching the opponents’ expectation before reflection.
rows.anchor: فجئ بان الذى للشك دون إذا الذي للوجوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concise فعل replaces the longer phrase bring a sūra like it, functioning as metonymic abbreviation.
rows.anchor: وعبر عن الاتيان بالفعل لأنه فعل من الأفعال والفائدة فيه أنه جار مجرى الكناية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولن تفعلوا is a parenthetical with no syntactic position; it cuts off the hesitation suggested by the conditional.
rows.anchor: ولا محل لقوله ولن تفعلوا لأنها جملة اعتراضية وحسن هذا الاعتراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khalil derives لن from لا أن.
rows.anchor: وعن الخليل أصلها لا أن

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ says لن is لا with its alif changed to nūn.
rows.anchor: وعند الفراء لا أبدلت الفها نونا

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh calls لن a particle emphasizing future negation.
rows.anchor: وعند سيبويه حرف موضع لتأكيد نفى المستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prediction is miraculous because any successful counter would have become famous, especially given the many critics and few defenders.
rows.anchor: لأنهم لو عارضوه بشئ لاشتهر فكيف والطاعنون فيه اكثر عددا من الذابين عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Failure to produce a comparable sūra establishes the Messenger’s truth; if they then refuse submission, they deserve the Fire.
rows.anchor: إذا لم يأتوا بها وتبين عجزهم عن المعارضة صح عندهم صدق الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear the Fire stands metonymically for abandoning obstinacy, since leaving denial is the means of avoiding punishment.
rows.anchor: فوضع فاتقوا النار موضعه لأن اتقاء النار سبب ترك العناد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وقود means what feeds a fire, namely firewood; as a verbal noun it is usually with ḍamma, though fatḥ is also attested.
rows.anchor: والوقود ما ترفع به النار يعنى الحطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause assumes the audience knows this Fire, perhaps from the People of the Book, the Messenger, or the earlier Meccan verse 66:6.
rows.anchor: وصلة الذى والتى يجب أن تكون معلوما للمخاطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The audience may have heard of the Fire from the People of the Book, the Messenger, or the earlier Meccan warning in 66:6; the definite wording recalls that prior disclosure.
rows.anchor: فيحتمل أن يكونوا سمعوا من أهل الكتاب أو من رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire is distinctive because it burns people and stones; sulfur stones burn intensely, cool slowly, smell foul, and cling to the body.
rows.anchor: ومعنى قوله تعالى وقودها الناس والحجارة أنها نار ممتازة عن غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the stones are idols; pairing idolaters with the objects they worship increases their regret because they made them partners of God.
rows.anchor: أو الأصنام المعبودة فهى أشد تحسيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pairing recalls 21:98, which calls the people and what they worship besides God fuel for Hell.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إنكم وما تعبدون من دون الله ﴾ حصب جهنم أى حطبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire’s having been prepared indicates that it is created.
rows.anchor: هيئت لهم فيه دليل على أن النار مخلوقة

rows.speaker: جهم
rows.claim: The author rejects Jahm’s view that the Fire is uncreated, taking its preparation as evidence that it is created.
rows.anchor: دليل على أن النار مخلوقة خلافا لما يقوله جهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God pairs encouragement with warning to motivate deeds that bring nearness and deter harmful conduct.
rows.anchor: سنة الله فى كتابه أن يذكر الترغيب مع الترهيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question expresses denial and astonishment: how disbelieve when the account gives reasons to believe? It resembles asking whether someone can fly without wings.
rows.anchor: معنى الهمزة التى في كيف مثله فى قولك اتكفرون بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were lifeless sperm drops in their fathers’ loins; ميت can also describe anything devoid of life, as in 25:49.
rows.anchor: نطفا فى أصلاب آبائكم والواو للحال وقد مضمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw is circumstantial with قد understood; أموات is the plural of ميت, like أقوال from قول.
rows.anchor: والاموات جمع ميت كالأقوال جمع قول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives life in the womb, causes death when lifetimes end, and raises people for resurrection.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فأحياكم ﴾ فى الأرحام ﴿ ثم يميتكم ﴾ عند انقضاء آجالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Return may mean arrival at recompense; alternatively the second life is in the graves and the return is resurrection.
rows.anchor: فى قبوركم ثم إليه ترجعون للنشور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa marks the immediate first life, while thumma marks the delays before death, the second life, and return to judgment.
rows.anchor: لأن الإحياء الأول قد تعقب الموت بلا تراخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account contains clear signs that should turn people away from disbelief and great blessings that should be thanked, not denied.
rows.anchor: حقها أن تشكر ولا تكفر

words: خَلَقَ لَكُم مَّا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created earthly things for worldly and religious benefit: their marvels disclose a wise Creator, and pleasures and hardships recall afterlife reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: أى لأجلكم ولا نتفاعكم به فى دنياكم ودينكم اما الأول فظاهر

rows.speaker: الكرخي وأبو بكر الرازي والمعتزلة
rows.claim: Al-Karkhi, Abu Bakr al-Razi, and the Muʿtazila infer that beneficial things were originally permissible from God’s creating them for people.
rows.anchor: وقد استدل الكرخى و أبو بكر الرازي والمعتزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جميعا is an accusative circumstantial qualifier of ما.
rows.anchor: ﴿ جميعا ﴾ نصب على الحال من ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: استوى means becoming straight and upright; with إلى it means directly intending the heavens without turning aside.
rows.anchor: الاستواء الاعتدال والاستقامة يقال استوى العود أى قام واعتدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: السماء here means the upper directions, so استوى إليها means turned toward what is above.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالسماء جهات العلو كأنه قيل ثم استوى إلى فوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun هنّ is ambiguous and explained by سبع سماوات, or refers to السماء, a singular used generically with plural meaning.
rows.anchor: مبهم يفسره ﴿ سبع سماوات ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making the heavens even means either removing crookedness and fissures or completing their creation.
rows.anchor: ومعنى تسويتهن تعديل خلقن وتقويمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma marks the greater rank of creating the heavens. This does not conflict with 79:30: earth’s body came first but its spreading came later.
rows.anchor: لأن جرم الأرض تقدم خلقه خلق السماء وأما دحوها فمتأخر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan describes earth at Jerusalem as a stone-like mass with clinging smoke; God raised the smoke to form the heavens, kept the mass in place, and spread earth from it.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن خلق الله الأرض فى موضع بيت المقدس كهيئة الفهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account is linked to 21:30, where heaven and earth are described as joined together.
rows.anchor: ﴿ كانتا رتقا ﴾ وهو الالتزاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the heavens perfectly and ordered earthly creation according to its inhabitants’ needs and benefits.
rows.anchor: فمن ثم خلقهن خلقا مستويا محكما من غير تفاوت

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وعلي
rows.claim: The segment contrasts a Medinan reading except Warsh with Abu ʿAmr and ʿAli, who treat the waw in وهو and its sisters as part of the word, like عضد.
rows.anchor: وهو وأخواته مدنى غير ورش وهو هو و أبو عمرو وعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before Adam, jinn inhabited earth and corrupted it; angels expelled them to islands, seas, and mountaintops, then settled there.
rows.anchor: لما خلق الله تعالى الأرض أسكن فيها الجن وأسكن فى السماء الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذ is governed by an omitted imperative, اذكر, meaning recall the story.
rows.anchor: إذ نصب باضمار اذكر والملائكة جمع ملاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ملائكة is the plural of ملاك, like شمائل from شمأل.
rows.anchor: والملائكة جمع ملاك كالشمائل جمع شمأل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جاعل means making or appointing, from a verb taking two objects: خليفة and في الأرض.
rows.anchor: من جعل الذى له مفعولان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A khalifa succeeds another; the feminine-pattern form has a hāʾ added for emphasis.
rows.anchor: وهو من يخلف غيره فعيله بمعنى فاعلة وزيدت الهاء للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The khalifa may mean a successor to the angels, who had inhabited earth before Adam and his descendants.
rows.anchor: والمعنى خليفة منكم لأنهم كانوا سكان الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may refer specifically to Adam, whose mention stands for his descendants, or generally to one who succeeds the angels.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل خلاف أو خلفاء لأنه أريد بالخليفة آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively Adam is God’s vicegerent on earth, as every prophet is; the author cites God’s address to David in 38:26.
rows.anchor: أو خليفة منى لأن آدم كان خليفة الله فى أرضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God informed the angels either to elicit a question and reveal the appointment’s wisdom or to teach people to consult before acting, though God needs no counsel.
rows.anchor: فيعرفوا حكمته فى استخلافهم قبل كونهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels wondered that obedient inhabitants would be replaced by sinners, while affirming God’s wisdom and knowledge.
rows.anchor: تعجب من أن يستخلف مكان أهل الطاعة أهل المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels knew through God’s information, the Preserved Tablet, or analogy between the two kinds of beings.
rows.anchor: أو من جهة اللوح أو قاسوا أحد الثقلين على الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يسفك means to pour or shed blood.
rows.anchor: أى يصب والواو فى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw in ونحن is circumstantial, and بحمدك is also circumstantial: the angels glorify while praising God.
rows.anchor: فى موضع الحال أى نسبح حامدين لك ومتلبسين بحمدك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction is like 5:61, where entering with disbelief means entering while disbelieving.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى ﴿ وقد دخلوا بالكفر ﴾ أى دخلوا كافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نقدس لك means purifying ourselves for God; alternatively tasbih and taqdis mean declaring God free of evil, with a root sense of going away and distancing.
rows.anchor: ونطهر أنفسنا لك وقيل التسبيح والتقديس تبعيد الله من السوء

words: قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows hidden wisdom: among humans will be prophets, saints, and scholars, along with matters the angels do not know.
rows.anchor: يعنى يكون فيهم الأنبساء و الأولياء والعلماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما is a relative pronoun and object of أعلم, with its antecedent omitted.
rows.anchor: وما بمعنى الذى وهو مفعول أعلم والعائد محذوف

rows.speaker: الحجازيون وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: The segment attributes a reading of إني to the Hijazis and Abu ʿAmr.
rows.anchor: إنى حجازى و أبو عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جهرة means seeing openly and plainly; it is a cognate accusative or a circumstantial accusative meaning visibly.
rows.anchor: عيانا وانتصابها على المصدر كما تنصب القرفصاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author glosses الصاعقة as death; another account says it was fire from heaven that burned them.
rows.anchor: أى الموت قيل هى نار جاءت من السماء فأحرقتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says seventy with Moses at the mountain claimed not to have worshipped the calf, demanded sight of God, then challenged Moses and were burned by lightning.
rows.anchor: روى أن السبعين الذين كانوا مع موسى عليه السلام عند الانطلاق إلى الجبل قالوا له نحن لم نعبد العجل

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila argue that punishment for demanding to see God proves that God cannot be seen.
rows.anchor: وتعلقت المعتزلة بهذه الآية فى نفى الرؤية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects that inference: they were punished for disbelief, including saying Moses had seen God and refusing faith until they saw openly.
rows.anchor: قلنا إنما عوقبوا بكفرهم لأن قولهم إنك رأيت الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They also withheld belief in Moses after his miracle appeared; prophets must be believed after miracles, and signs should not be demanded out of obstinacy.
rows.anchor: ولأنهم امتنعوا عن الإيمان بموسى بعد ظهور معجزته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They watched the lightning descend.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأنتم تنظرون ﴾ اليها حين نزلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They chose worldly life over the afterlife, as a buyer chooses what to purchase.
rows.anchor: اختاروها على الآخرة اختيار المشترى

words: فَلَا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ وَلَا هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment will not be lightened, and no one will defend them by driving it away.
rows.anchor: ولا ينصرهم أحد بالدفع عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naskh linguistically means replacement; legally it declares the end of a ruling understood by us as continuing, so it replaces for us but clarifies for the Lawgiver.
rows.anchor: تفسير النسخ لغة التبديل وشريعة بيان انتهاء الحكم الشرعى المطلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This account answers the charge of badaʾ made by Jews who deny abrogation: God clarifies a ruling’s end rather than changing His knowledge.
rows.anchor: وفيه جواب عن البداء الذى يدعيه منكروه أعنى اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abrogation applies to a ruling possible in itself and lacking an explicit or implied time limit or declaration of permanence.
rows.anchor: ومحله حكم يحتمل الوجود والعدم فى نفسه لم يلحق به ما ينافى النسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Valid abrogation requires ability to form inward commitment, not ability to act; the author rejects the Muʿtazila’s added condition.
rows.anchor: وشرطه التمكن من عقد القلب عندنا دون التمكن من الفعل خلافا للمعتزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abrogation may occur through Qur’an or Sunna, whether the sources agree or differ.
rows.anchor: يجوز النسخ بالكتاب والسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author permits abrogating recitation and ruling together, the ruling alone, or the recitation alone.
rows.anchor: ويجوز نسخ التلاوة والحكم والحكم دون التلاوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abrogating a description through a ruling, such as adding to a text, counts as abrogation for the author, contrary to al-Shafiʿi.
rows.anchor: ونسخ وصف بالحكم مثل الزيادة على النص فإنه نسخ عندنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making a verse forgotten means removing it from people’s memory.
rows.anchor: والانساء أن يذهب بحفظها عن القلوب

rows.speaker: مكي وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Makki and Abu ʿAmr read ننسأها, from نسأت, meaning to defer it.
rows.anchor: مكى و أبو عمرو أى نؤخرها من نسأت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A better replacement benefits people because acting on it earns greater reward.
rows.anchor: نأت بآية خير منها للعباد أى بآية العمل بها أكثر للثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A replacement may instead be equal in this respect, since no Qur’anic verse is superior to another.
rows.anchor: فى ذلك إذ لا فضيلة لبعض الآيات على البعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer asks for a messenger from the Muslim community itself; God sent Muhammad among them.
rows.anchor: من أنفسهم فبعث الله فيهم محمدا عليه السلام

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet said he was the prayer of his father Abraham, the glad tidings of Jesus, and his mother’s vision; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام انا دعوة ابى إبراهيم وبشرى عيسى ورؤيا امى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger recites and conveys God’s revelation: proofs of divine oneness and the truthfulness of prophets and messengers.
rows.anchor: يقرأ عليهم ويبلغهم ما توحى إليه من دلائل وحدانيتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book is the Qur’an; wisdom is the Sunna and understanding the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: ﴿ والحكمة ﴾ السنة وفهم القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purifying them means cleansing them of associating partners with God and other defilements.
rows.anchor: ويطهرهم من الشرك وسائر الأرجاس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: العزيز is the invincible one who cannot be overcome; الحكيم describes God’s wisdom in what He grants.
rows.anchor: الغالب الذى لا يغلب ﴿ الحكيم ﴾ فيما أوليت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كتب means prescribed as an obligation.
rows.anchor: فرض ﴿ عليكم إذا حضر أحدكم الموت ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death’s arrival means it has drawn near and its signs have appeared.
rows.anchor: أى إذا دنا منه فظهرت أمارته

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali glosses خير as abundant wealth; he stopped a client with only seven hundred from bequeathing, saying this was not enough.
rows.anchor: روى عن على رضى الله عنه أن مولى له أراد أن يوصى وله سبعمائة فمنعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says bequests to heirs were required early in Islam, then abrogated by inheritance verses, as explained in Sharh al-Manar.
rows.anchor: وكانت للوارث فى بدء الإسلام فنسخت بآية المواريث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view keeps the verse for non-inheriting relatives, including non-Muslim parents of new Muslims; a recommended bequest maintains kinship, and كتب then does not mean obligatory.
rows.anchor: وقيل هى غير منسوخة لانها نزلت فى حق من ليس بوارث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fair bequest neither favors the rich while leaving the poor nor exceeds one-third.
rows.anchor: بالعدل وهو أن لا يوصى للغنى ويدع الفقير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حقا is an emphatic verbal noun; the God-fearing here are those who avoid associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: مصدر مؤكد أى حق ذلك حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: شهر رمضان is a subject with the relative clause as predicate; alternatively it is an appositive to الصيام or a predicate after omitted هو.
rows.anchor: مبتدأ خبره ﴿ الذي أنزل فيه القرآن ﴾ أى ابتدى فيه إنزاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s revelation began in Ramadan on the Night of Decree; alternatively the verse was revealed about the fasting duty in 2:183.
rows.anchor: وكان ذلك فى ليلة القدر أو أنزل فى شأنه القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ramadan derives from رمض, burning from hot ground; it became the month’s name and is indeclinable because it is definite and ends in ألف ونون. The name recalls hunger’s hardship or seasonal heat.
rows.anchor: والرمضان مصدر رمض إذا احترق من الرمضاء فأضيف إليه الشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the hadith صام رمضان, شهر is omitted from شهر رمضان; the omission is understood from context and causes no ambiguity.
rows.anchor: هو من باب الحذف لا من الإلباس

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makki reads القرآن without hamza.
rows.anchor: القرآن حيث كان غير مهموز مكى

words: هُدًۭى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَٰتٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْهُدَىٰ وَٱلْفُرْقَانِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هدى and بينات are circumstantial accusatives: the Qur’an was sent as guidance, with clear signs distinguishing truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: على الحال أى أنزل وهو هداية للناس إلى الحق

words: هُدًۭى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَٰتٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْهُدَىٰ وَٱلْفُرْقَانِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These signs belong to God’s guidance through revelation and heavenly books, distinguishing truth from falsehood and guidance from error.
rows.anchor: ذكر أولا أنه هدى ثم ذكر أنه بينات من جملة ما هدى به الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone present and resident during the month must fast it; a traveler need not fast while traveling.
rows.anchor: فمن كان شاهدا أى حاضرا مقيما غير مسافر فى الشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الشهر and the pronoun in ليصمه are temporal adverbials, not direct objects, since residents and travelers both witness the month.
rows.anchor: والشهر منصوب على الظرف وكذا الهاء فى ليصمه

words: وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍۢ فَعِدَّةٌۭ مِّنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sick and traveler may defer fasting and make up an equal number of days later; عدة is a subject with its predicate omitted.
rows.anchor: فعدة مبتدأ والخبر محذوف أى فعليه عدة

words: يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلْعُسْرَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allowing the sick and traveler to break the fast expresses the intended ease.
rows.anchor: حيث أباح الفطر بالسفر والمرض

words: وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects requiring sick people and travelers to break the fast and repeat it if they fast, since that contradicts the stated ease.
rows.anchor: ومن فرض الفطر على المريض والمسافر حتى لو صاما تجب عليهما الإعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The causal verb is omitted but supplied by the preceding clause; completing the count explains the instruction to make up missed days.
rows.anchor: والفعل المعلل محذوف مدلول عليه بما سبق تقديره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Completing the count is the reason to make up missed days.
rows.anchor: فقوله لتكملوا علة الأمر بمراعاة العدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Magnifying God explains the way to discharge the missed-fast obligation through makeup.
rows.anchor: ولتكبروا علة ما علم من كيفية القضاء والخروج من عهدة الفطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hope of gratitude explains the concession to break the fast; this is a subtle form of لف.
rows.anchor: ولعلكم تشكرون علة الترخيص وهذا نوع من اللف اللطيف المسلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: على accompanies magnification because it carries the sense of praise: magnify God while praising Him for guidance.
rows.anchor: وعدى التكبير بعلى لتضمنه معنى الحمد كأنه قيل لتكبروا الله

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr reads لتكملوا with a doubled mīm.
rows.anchor: ولتكملوا بالتشديد أبو بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After finishing the acts prescribed in pilgrimage and departing, people should remember God.
rows.anchor: فإذا فرغتم من عباداتكم التى أمرتم بها فى الحج ونفرتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remember God abundantly, as people recounted and boasted of their ancestors’ merits and achievements.
rows.anchor: فأكثروا من ذكر الله وبالغوا فيه كما تفعلون فى ذكر آبائكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After pilgrimage, Arabs gathered between the mosque at Mina and the mountain to recount ancestors’ virtues and famous days.
rows.anchor: وكانوا إذا قضوا مناسكهم وقفوا بين المسجد بمنى وبين الجبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أشد ذكرا means more abundant remembrance; grammatically أشد is genitive by coordination and ذكرا is specification.
rows.anchor: أى أكثر وهو فى موضع جر عطف على ما أضيف إليه الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison is to Quraysh’s remembrance of ancestors or to a people who surpassed them in it.
rows.anchor: كذكر قريش آباءهم أو قوم أشد منهم ذكرا وذكرا تمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among pilgrims are people who ask God only for worldly advantages.
rows.anchor: فمن الذين يشهدون الحج من يسأل الله حظوظ الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask for worldly giving alone, especially status and wealth.
rows.anchor: اجعل إتياننا أى إعطاءنا فى الدنيا خاصة يعنى الجاه والغنى

words: وَمَا لَهُۥ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَٰقٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They have no afterlife share because, as disbelievers, their concern is confined to worldly life; believers should seek both worlds, as in 2:201.
rows.anchor: نصيب لأن همه مقصور على الدنيا لكفره بالآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author recounts the stages: the first Meccan verse (16:67) allowed intoxicants; after Umar and others asked about wine’s harm, this verse followed. Some drank and others abstained.
rows.anchor: نزل فى الخمر أربع آيات نزل بمكة ومن ثمرات النخيل والأعناب تتخذون منه سكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After this verse, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf hosted drinkers; an intoxicated imam misrecited the disavowal sūra, prompting 4:43’s ban on approaching prayer while drunk.
rows.anchor: ثم دعا عبد الرحمن ابن عوف جماعة فشربوا وسكروا وأم بعضهم فقرأ قل يا أيها الكافرون

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: After ʿUtban ibn Malik’s guests became drunk, argued, and fought, Umar prayed for a clear ruling; 5:90 followed and he said they abstained.
rows.anchor: ثم دعا عتبان بن مالك جماعة فلما سكروا منها تخاصموا وتضاربوا فقال عمر اللهم بين لنا

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali said that if wine fell into a well he would not call prayer from a minaret built there, nor graze land exposed by a dried sea where it had fallen.
rows.anchor: وعن على رضى الله عنه لو وقعت قطرة فى بئر فبنيت مكانها منارة لم أؤذن عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khamr is grape juice that boils, intensifies, and foams; its name means covering because it veils the mind.
rows.anchor: والخمر ما غلى واشتد وقذف بالزبد من عصير العنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maysir is gambling, from يسر; it may be named for taking wealth easily without effort or for depriving someone of wealth.
rows.anchor: والميسر القمار مصدر من يسر كالموعد من فعله يقال يسرته إذا قمرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The traditional game used ten arrows: al-fadh, taw'am, raqib, hils, nafis, musbil, and muʿalla awarded one to seven shares; manih, safih, and waghd were blanks.
rows.anchor: وصفة الميسر أنه كانت لهم عشرة أقداح سبعة منها عليها خطوط وهو الفذ وله سهم والتوأم وله سهمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An impartial arbiter drew arrows from a bag; winners took their marked share, while blank-drawers got nothing and paid the camel’s full cost.
rows.anchor: فيجعلون الأقداح فى خريطة ويضعونها على يد عدل ثم يجلجلها ويدخل يده ويخرج باسم رجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Winners gave shares to the poor, did not eat them, boasted of generosity, and disparaged those who declined to gamble.
rows.anchor: وكانوا يدفعون تلك الأنصباء إلى الفقراء ولا يأكلون منها ويفتخرون بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ruling includes all forms of gambling, such as backgammon and chess.
rows.anchor: وفى حكم الميسر أنواع القمار من النرد والشطرنج وغيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question concerns the consequences of participating in drinking and gambling, as shown by the answer about sin and benefits.
rows.anchor: والمعنى يسألونك عما فى تعاطيهما بدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their sin includes quarrels, insults, obscene speech, and falsehood.
rows.anchor: بسبب التخاصم والتشاتم وقول الفحش والزور

rows.speaker: حمزة وعلي
rows.claim: Hamza and ʿAli read كثير, meaning many, in place of كبير.
rows.anchor: كثير حمزة وعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wine benefits include trade and drinking pleasure; gambling may benefit the poor or bring easy money.
rows.anchor: بالتجارة فى الخمر والتلذذ بشربها وفى الميسر بارتفاق الفقراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their sin outweighs their benefit because drinkers and gamblers commit sins in many ways.
rows.anchor: لأن أصحاب الشرب والقمار يقترفون فيهما الآثام من وجوه كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿafw is surplus beyond need; early Muslims had to donate surplus after retaining a year’s provisions as farmers or a day’s as artisans, until the zakat verse abrogated the rule.
rows.anchor: أى الفضل أى أنفقوا ما فضل عن قدر الحاجة وكان التصدق بالفضل فى أول الإسلام فرضا

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr reads العفو in the accusative; then ماذا is one noun as the object and the answer means they spend the surplus.
rows.anchor: أبو عمرو فمن نصبه جعل ماذا اسما واحدا فى موضع النصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ما is the subject and ذا a relative pronoun with ينفقون as its clause, the answer العفو matches the question’s nominative syntax.
rows.anchor: ومن رفعه جعل ما مبتدأ وخبره ذا مع صلته فذا بمعنى الذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kāf in كذلك modifies an omitted verbal noun in the accusative: an explanation like this explanation.
rows.anchor: الكاف فى موضع نصب نعت لمصدر محذوف

words: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِى حَآجَّ إِبْرَٰهِۦمَ فِى رَبِّهِۦٓ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God consoles the Prophet by recalling Abraham’s dispute with Nimrod, who claimed lordship.
rows.anchor: ثم عجب نبيه عليه السلام وسلاه بمجادلة إبراهيم عليه السلام نمرود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in Abraham’s Lord may refer to Abraham or to the arguer; either way the two share one Lord.
rows.anchor: والهاء فى ربه يرجع إلى إبراهيم أو الذى حاج فهو ربهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may mean kingship made Nimrod arrogant and caused the dispute, used against the Muʿtazila on aṣlaḥ; alternatively the dispute occurred when kingship was given.
rows.anchor: لأن آتاه الله يعنى أن إيتاء الملك أبطره وأورثه الكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذ is an adverb governed by يحاج or a substitute for أن آتاه when that phrase means at the time.
rows.anchor: نصب يحاج أو بدل من أن آتاه إذا جعل بمعنى الوقت

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: The segment attributes a reading of إبراهيم ربي to Hamza.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إبراهيم ربي ﴾ حمزة ﴿ الذي يحيى ويميت ﴾ كأنه قال له من ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham answers the question about his Lord by saying He is the one who gives life and death.
rows.anchor: كأنه قال له من ربك قال ربى الذي يحيى ويميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nimrod claimed to give life and death by pardoning one condemned to die and killing another.
rows.anchor: يريد أعفى عن القتل وأقتل فانقطع اللعين بهذا

words: فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْتِى بِٱلشَّمْسِ مِنَ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham did not abandon a valid first proof; because Nimrod distorted it out of obstinacy, Abraham gave an argument that could not mislead the weak-minded.
rows.anchor: وهذا ليس بانتقال من حجة إلى حجة كما زعم البعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These astrologers knew the sun’s motion; God forces it against its apparent direction, so a claimant to divinity should be able to reverse it.
rows.anchor: وكانوا أهل تنجيم وحركة الكواكب من المغرب إلى المشرق معلومة لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forced movement is likened to water carrying an ant on a millstone opposite its own direction.
rows.anchor: كتحريك الماء النمل على الرحى إلى غير جهة حركة النمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbeliever was bewildered and stunned.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فبهت الذي كفر ﴾ تحير ودهش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not guide wrongdoers means that He does not grant them success.
rows.anchor: أى لا يوفقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say God diverted Nimrod from asking Abraham to bring the sun from the west; another says Nimrod claimed divinity and acknowledged no other lord.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه كان يدعى الربوبية لنفسه وما كان يعترف بالربوبية لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nimrod meant that he alone was the one to whom giving life and death could be attributed.
rows.anchor: ومعنى قوله انا أحيي وأميت أن الذى ينسب إليه

words: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِى حَآجَّ إِبْرَٰهِۦمَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse permits theological argument: Abraham debated, prophets do not commit forbidden acts, and inviting disbelievers requires answering their demand for proof.
rows.anchor: ولأنا أمرنا بدعاء الكفرة إلى الإيمان بالله وتوحيده

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَخْفَىٰ عَلَيْهِ شَىْءٌۭ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing in the world is hidden from God; He knows who disbelieves and who believes and will recompense each.
rows.anchor: أى فى العالم فعبر عنه بالسماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ورسولا may be joined to وجيها, supplied by omitted نجعله رسولا, or read as a circumstantial accusative describing Jesus as honored in both worlds.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ورسولا ﴾ أى ونجعله رسولا أو يكون فى موضع الحال

words: أَنِّى قَدْ جِئْتُكُم بِـَٔايَةٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أنى introduces the content as that I have come to you with a sign.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قد جئتكم بآية من ربكم ﴾ بدلالة تدل على صدقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sign is proof that Jesus’ claim to prophethood is true.
rows.anchor: بدلالة تدل على صدقي فيما أدعيه من النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أنّي أخلق may be accusative as substitute for أني قد جئتكم, genitive as substitute for آية, or nominative after omitted هي.
rows.anchor: نصب بدل من أنى قد جئتكم أو جر بدل من آية

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: The segment notes Nafiʿ’s resumptive reading.
rows.anchor: أو رفع على هى أنى أخلق لم أنى نافع على الاستئناف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus shapes from clay an object resembling a bird.
rows.anchor: أى اقدر لكم شيئا مثل صورة الطير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in فيه refers to the kāf of كهيئة: Jesus breathes into the thing resembling a bird.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فأنفخ فيه ﴾ الضمير للكاف أى فى ذلك الشئ

rows.speaker: مدني
rows.claim: The Medinan reading adds طائرا, describing the resulting bird as flying like other birds.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فيكون طيرا ﴾ فيصير طيرا كسائر الطيور طائرا مدنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By God’s permission means by His command; the author also reports that Jesus created no creature except the bat.
rows.anchor: ﴿ بإذن الله ﴾ بأمره قيل لم يخلق شيئا غير الخفاش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The akmah is someone born blind.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأبرئ الأكمه ﴾ الذى ولد أعمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating by God’s permission prevents anyone from imagining Jesus possessed divinity.
rows.anchor: كرر بإذن الله دفعا لوهم من يتوهم فيه اللاهوتية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Jesus raised Shem, Noah’s son, before onlookers; when they called it magic and asked for a sign, he told them what they had eaten and stored.
rows.anchor: فقالوا هذا سحر مبين فأرنا آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In both clauses, ما may be a relative pronoun or a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وما فيهما بمعنى الذى أو مصدرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All the preceding signs are evidence for the Israelites if they believe.
rows.anchor: لآية لكم إن كنتم مؤمنين
